bc_yonderland.blurb: Yonderland is a west-facing sport crag in the Squamish area, a short distance around the corner from Fern Hill. A steep trail with switchbacks and fixed ropes leads up to a ledge below the routes, so it is not a spot for small children. Lines reach about 20 m and are mostly 5.10 to 5.11, with technical, crimpy sequences on bulges and overhangs. Some of the rock is still loose, so a helmet is a good idea. The wall stays shaded until around 2 pm, then gets sun, and a steady breeze usually keeps it comfortable.
bc_yonderland.parking_note: Leave the car in the large Fern Hill lot at the end of Powerhouse Springs Forest Service Road.
bc_yonderland.approach: About 1.4 km from the lot on the Far Side trail: roughly ten switchbacks, then a slope climbed with fixed ropes to the ledge below the routes. Allow 20 to 25 minutes on foot, or about 10 by bike.

bc_coho_park.blurb: Coho Park is a wooded city park in Squamish, set between the Garibaldi Estates and Garibaldi Highlands neighbourhoods. Small outcrops sit alongside the trail, and the bouldering here is easy to moderate: nine problems, mostly V0 and V1 with a single V2, with landings described as good. The setting is a ferny, mossy forest with a creek running through it, and the boulders are a short flat walk in, which makes it a handy spot for beginners or a quick session.

bc_neverland.blurb: Neverland is a sport crag in Squamish just off the east end of the Olympic Legacy Park parking lot, with almost no walk to reach it. Routes start around 5.9 and run up into the 5.12s, in varied, technical styles. The wall has scoops, bulges, cracks, seams and a few pockets. It sits in a small forest clearing among big sword ferns, and it is shaded in the morning and again late in the day, so midday tends to be the sunniest stretch. Works for a quick session or a full day of clipping bolts.
